By default, the successful candidate will be offered a contract in the MSF office, able to issue a contract, of their country of residence at the time of application. If no MSF office exists in their country of residence, the successful candidate will be expected to relocate to a country where an MSF office can issue a contract, provided the local legislation allows for that. MSF INTERNATIONAL Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) is an international, independent, medical humanitarian organisation that delivers emergency aid to people affected by armed conflict, epidemics, healthcare exclusion and natural disasters. MSF offers assistance to people based only on need and irrespective of race, religion, gender or political affiliation. MSF International is the legal entity that binds MSF’s 24 sections, 28 associations and 19 branch offices together. Registered in Switzerland, MSF International provides coordination, information and support to the MSF Movement, as well as implements international projects and initiatives as requested. SAFEGUARDING REQUIREMENTS FOR THE ROLE The incumbent commits to contribute to a safe, supportive, inclusive, equitable, diverse, respectful, and healthy workplace, and associative spaces free from abuse and other misconduct. They will not engage in any form of abuse including those detailed in MSF Typologies of Abuse and when an employee suspects or observes abuse, they will report it (without investigating it) to protect others. I. CONTEXT MSF is committed to creating a safe, respectful, and dignified environment for its patients, their caretakers, and the communities in which it works, and for all its volunteers and staff, board and associative members. To this end, all sections of MSF have adopted Behavioural Commitments designed to ensure all staff are aware of their obligations to create workspaces free from abuse and inappropriate behaviour. MSF is committed to safeguarding and ensuring zero tolerance of inaction on abuse. MSF is continuously strengthening its safeguarding work, and safeguarding remains a top organizational priority. In line with this organization commitment, MSF has created a Board Strengthening Programme, as well as Ethical Leadership Minimum Standards (ELMS) applicable to all board members. As safeguarding expands, MSF’s associative structure is working to adopt the highest standards of safeguarding for and amongst its members. II. PURPOSE OF THE JOB The Safeguarding and Ethical Leadership Coordinator for Boards and Associations supports the implementation, operationalisation, monitoring, and continuous improvement of MSF’s safeguarding work with boards and associations across the MSF movement. This reflects the International Board’s commitment to minimum standards for safeguarding in associative networks. The Role: leads coordination and implementation efforts that translate safeguarding principles, commitments, policies, and standards into practical, measurable, consistent, coherent, and sustainable safeguarding practices across MSF’s boards and associative structures. advances safeguarding culture change by supporting MSF boards in understanding their role in safeguarding leadership and oversight; and by supporting the development of robust safeguarding understanding and putting in place safeguarding measures within associative structures and associations. contributes to strengthening prevention, detection, reporting, response to safeguarding cases. promotes accountability and institutional learning on safeguarding across the MSF movement. III. ACCOUNTABILITIES Coordination, design, and implementation: Lead the coordination, implementation, and training on the ELMS, as well as on safeguarding, and other ethics principles within MSF boards. Translate safeguarding and ELMS concepts into actionable documents, processes, and initiatives for MSF boards associations/networks in line with existing MSF initiatives on safeguarding. Develop implementation guidance, tools, frameworks, templates, and operational resources. Key Accountabilities: Safeguarding ambitions are translated into practical implementation plans and deliverables. Implementation progress is systematically tracked, monitored, and reported. Approaches, tools, trainings, and guidance are developed and used by relevant stakeholders. Drive safeguarding culture change: Drive integration of safeguarding as a core organizational practice across MSF boards and associations. Strengthen safeguarding accountability and leadership engagement, and ownership. Other tasks assigned by the ISC or the International President or their delegate. Lead monitoring, accountability, learning, and continuous improvement on Safeguarding and Ethical Governance: Monitor implementation progress, identify risks and gaps, and drive corrective and improvement actions where needed. Analyze ELMS and safeguarding implementation, challenges, and lessons learned to inform strategic decision-making. Produce implementation reports, dashboards, briefing papers, presentations, and governance updates. Lead learning and knowledge-sharing initiatives related to safeguarding and ELMS implementation and best practices. Key Accountabilities: Safeguarding is embedded into MSF associations and boards’ ways of working. Safeguarding considerations are integrated into associative and boards’ processes. Organisational awareness and ownership of safeguarding responsibilities is increased across the MSF associations and boards. Coordinate the framework and response to ELMS and safeguarding complaints involving senior leadership: Ensure relevant frameworks and processes relating to triage, case management, investigation, and decision-making are implemented for ELMS and safeguarding complaints involving senior leadership (the incumbent will not engage, case management, investigations or decision-making directly, but rather ensure it is in place). Reception, and coordination, initial review and assessment of safeguarding and ELMs allegations involving senior leadership (i.e. General Directors and board members). Ensure a decision-making panel is formed for ELMS-related complaints, and ensure their decision is reported to the International Board. Key Accountabilities: Ensure that ELMs related complaints are properly assigned to relevant experts for case management/investigation. Ensure a decision-making panel is formed for safeguarding or ELMs-related complaints, and ensure their decision is reported to the International Board. AUTONOMY, COMPLEXITY The Role Is Responsible Under The Technical Supervision Of The ISC And The Hierarchical Supervision Of The International President (or The IP’s Delegate). The Role Will Coordinate Closely With: the Board Strengthening Programme concerning board training and direct board support activities with respect to safeguarding and ELMS implementation. the International Associative Team to ensure appropriate association support and training activities with respect to safeguarding. the ILD to ensure legal risks and statutory requirements are duly considered. The role uses subject matter expertise, analysis, independent judgement and translates safeguarding, and ethical governance initiatives (such as the Ethical Leadership and Minimum Standards), and other safeguarding initiatives and concepts into relatable, understood, actionable documents, trainings, and actionable initiatives that support to ensure all parts of MSF have a robust understanding of, and structures that support safeguarding. The role needs a strong understanding of, safeguarding policies, codes of conducts-including ethical governance principles, and how to draft them for associations (non-staff), alongside an understanding of the role of trustees and Boards as oversight for safeguarding. The incumbent will also need to understand case management and administrative investigations to be able to explain these concepts and how they relate to oversight and associations. The incumbent will also need to have good understanding of confidentiality, and act with the utmost discretion, when following up, and arranging that safeguarding and ELMs complaints involving senior leadership are properly and promptly addressed. REQUIREMENTS Education A master's degree in relevant field such as law, human rights, administration etc. Or a bachelor's degree combined with significant relevant experience in safeguarding, governance of non-profits. Experience A minimum of 5 years implementing safeguarding initiatives, especially with boards. Strong understanding of case management and administrative investigations in a workplace setting and principles guiding case management and ability to explain these concepts. Experience working with or as a board member for a non-profit organization. Experience drafting key safeguarding documents. Experience in designing and delivering safeguarding training. MSF experience is an asset. Knowledge / Skills Strong understanding of safeguarding, conflicts of interest and the role of a trustee/governance of non-profit organisations. Ability to draft appropriate and relevant safeguarding standards/documents and to translate complex concepts into clear actions. Ability to coordinate and work with a range of stakeholders in a consultative, diplomatic fashion. Strong writing skills and ability to communicate safeguarding concepts simply to a range of audiences. A strong understanding of monitoring and evaluation. Demonstrated experience in coordinating or overseeing highly sensitive cases involving senior leadership; receiving and appropriately triaging sensitive allegations; governance and due-process principles; management of conflicts of interest and recusal; commissioning and oversight of independent investigations; confidentiality, secure information management and data protection; whistleblowing and retaliation considerations; and the ability to navigate complex situations involving boards, senior executives, safeguarding and legal functions. Demonstrated ability to lead complex implementation and coordination initiatives across diverse stakeholders. Ability to influence organisational change in multicultural environments. Strong strategic coordination and implementation management skills. Perseverance and ability to build consensus. Independence of judgement and the ability to challenge senior stakeholders, when necessary, alongside diplomacy and consensus-building. Demonstrated ability to drive accountability and follow-through across multiple workstreams. Ability to navigate sensitive safeguarding issues with discretion, diplomacy, and sound judgement. Cross cultural awareness and strong commitment to and understanding of diversity, equity, and inclusion principles. Languages English, other languages are an asset, especially French and Spanish. Other Motivation to work in a humanitarian organisation and a fast paced, dynamic environment. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. Radio产品PCB全流程设计： 负责射频（RF）类产品的PCB设计全周期工作，包含PCB Layout（高频/高速信号布局布线）、DRC/LVS检查、生产文件输出（Gerber/NC Drill/IPC2581/ODB++等），了解熟悉PCB生产制造工艺，跟踪PCB制板及SMA过程，和相关人员配合协助完成PCBA整个流程确保设计满足射频性能、可靠性及量产要求。 2. 射频电路设计与优化： 主导射频产品（如PA、LNA、滤波器、天线接口等）的PCB设计，完成阻抗匹配、信号完整性（SI）、电源完整性（PI）分析给出经验设计，解决EMC/EMI问题（如辐射干扰、静电防护）。 3. 跨部门协作与问题解决： 与硬件工程师、射频工程师、结构散热工程师、SI/PI工程师、SMA团队、测试团队协作，解决PCB设计中的技术难点（如高频信号串扰、热管理、薄型化设计）量产爬坡及客诉问题分析，提出设计改进方案。 4. 英语沟通与应用： 独立阅读英文技术文档（如Datasheet、应用笔记），与国际团队（如海外研发中心、供应商）进行邮件/会议沟通。 任职要求 1. 基础资质：本科及以上学历，电子工程、通信工程、电磁场与微波技术等相关专业；5年以上Radio产品（如通信类RRU/MIMO、消费类射频产品）PCB设计经验，有成功量产项目案例优先。 2. 核心技术能力： 精通Cadence（Allegro）PCB设计工具，熟悉高频PCB层叠设计、高速信号（PCIE4.0以上、Eth112G经验优先）布局布线规则； 了解PCB制程工艺（如FR4/Teflon材料、HDI工艺、表面处理），能根据产品需求选择合适的板材、线宽/线距、过孔参数； 3. 软技能： 逻辑清晰，具备强问题分析与解决能力，能快速定位并推动解决设计中的技术瓶颈； 良好的英语读写与沟通能力（CET-6或同等水平），能熟练阅读英文技术资料并与海外团队协作； 团队协作意识强，具备跨部门沟通经验（如与结构、测试、供应链团队配合）。

review_candidates.description: Mechanical & Piping Superintendent - Ref. JOB-1503 Summary We are looking for a Mechanical & Piping Superintendent to join a large-scale industrial project in the energy sector. In this role, you will be responsible for supervising on-site mechanical and industrial piping installation activities, ensuring compliance with safety, quality, and schedulre requirements. You will play a key role in coordinating subcontractors, monitoring construction progress, and managing supervision teams, with both technical and managerial responsibilities. Your Responsibilities Supervise the installation of mechanical equipment and piping systems on site. Lead and coordinate subcontractors and supervision involved in your discipline. Manage interfaces with other site disciplines on site and actively participate in construction progress meetings. Ensure that all work complies with technical documentation, applicable standards, and contractual requirements. Contribute to the implementation and validation of quality plans and inspection & test plans (ITPs) in coordination with the project QA/QC manager. Identify and resolve technical issues related to mechanical and piping installation activities. Promote a strong safety culture and ensure strict compliance with HSE rules by all stakeholders. Monitor work progress, analyze deviations, and provide regular reports covering progress, quantities,forecasted costs. Review and validate final project documentation. Your Experience Minimum of 10 years' experience in mechanical and piping supervision on large industrial projects. Strong background in piping for sensitive services (oxygen and hydrogen). Demonstrated sucess in subcontractor management and multidisciplinary team coordination. YOUR PROFILE Technical degree in Mechanical Engineering or equivalent. Strong technical expertise in mechanical assembly and industrial piping installation. Leadership, autonomy, attention to detail and a strong sense of responsibility. Excellent communication and coordination skills. Professional proficiency in English, both written and spoken. YOUR MOTIVATION Not only are you an excellent Mechanical & Piping Superintendent, but you are committed to executing your project with minimal environmental impact. You strive to find cost-effective solutions to reduce the project's carbon footprint and minimize its impact on the project site. ALDEBARAN Group ALDEBARAN Group operates in the energy and infrastructure sectors, supporting clients in France and internationally. The company assists clients committed to reducing their carbon and environmental impact in the coming years, with the goal of achieving carbon neutrality as soon as possible. Similarly, we recruit the best technical and managerial profiles to help our client move in this direction as quickly as possible. This doesn't limit us to recruiting environmental specialists, but we consider carbon neutrality an essential part of their business.
